title: security(rbac-v2,kms): enforce KMS region pinning + audit logging backfill
author: Ava Nguyen
release_notes: Enforces KMS region pinning at policy evaluation time, adds audit log fields for kms_region, and backfills missing audit records. No user-visible API changes when feature flag disabled. Migration required.
description:
Context: customer audits and internal compliance reviews uncovered gaps in how RBAC v2 policies interacted with KMS region constraints. Some services were allowed to create keys or bind resources without an explicit kms_region tag, and audit logs did not consistently record the effective kms_region used for key operations. This PR enforces kms_region pinning at policy-evaluation time, augments audit entries with kms_region metadata, and provides a backfill migration for historical audit records where region can be inferred.

What I changed: 1) Policy evaluator: require kms_region constraint evaluation for KMS-related actions and return a clear denial reason when missing. 2) Audit pipeline: attach kms_region to outbound audit events (producer side) and update schema compatibility guards. 3) Migrations: SQL migration to add kms_region column (nullable) to audits table plus a backfill job that infers region from existing key metadata (best-effort). 4) Feature flag: gated behind feature flag "rbac_v2_kms_region_pinning" for staged rollout. 5) Tests & docs: unit/integration tests for evaluator and audit enrichment, and a short doc on rollout/migration steps.

Motivation: this improves data residency guarantees and makes it possible to reliably enforce region pinning for enterprise customers that require KMS residency. It also closes an audit gap by recording the effective kms_region on key access events.

Deployment plan: - Merge on main (this PR) - Enable feature flag in staging and run backfill on staging exports - Smoke tests for RBAC and KMS operations - Roll feature flag to canary customers with Dedicated instances - Full rollout after 72h of no regressions. The backfill is additive and safe to run multiple times.

Migration notes: new nullable column audits.kms_region. Backfill attempts to infer from key_id -> key metadata API; entries that cannot be inferred remain null. Backfill has a throttled job that runs per-tenant over 24-72h depending on data size. We included a dry-run mode.

Testing: included unit tests for policy evaluator, integration test that exercises a denial path when kms_region missing, and an end-to-end test for audit enrichment. CI initially failed on a flaky storage test, rerun passed.

Checklist: - [x] Policy evaluator changes - [x] Audit schema migration + backfill job - [x] Feature flag gating - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs and rollout notes - [x] Security review (SEC-211 referenced)

tests: integration test for kms_region denial path and audit enrichment

review_comments: Carlos Mendez: Can we make the denial message consumable by the SDKs so clients can present actionable errors? (requested change)
Ava Nguyen: Responded that evaluator now returns structured denial reason code 'KMS_REGION_MISSING' and a human message; SDK mapping added in sdk-python (follow-up PR).
Priya Patel: Requested more robust backfill error handling for rate-limited key metadata APIs. Ava: added exponential backoff and per-tenant throttling; added dry-run mode and failure logs.

Liam O'Connor: Asked about performance impact on policy evaluation hot-path. Ava: added bench micro-optimizations and a cache for per-request key metadata lookups; observed <2% p95 latency impact in load test.
ci_checks: ci/unit-tests: failed (storage-emulator-timeout) on first run -> rerun passed
notes_for_ops: Run migration: bin/rails db:migrate VERSION=20260220 then trigger backfill in dry-run mode first.
Backfill: run services/audit/jobs/backfill_kms_region.py --dry-run to validate and then without flag to apply; monitor job logs for rate-limit errors.
Feature flag: enable rbac_v2_kms_region_pinning in staging first (ops/featureflags/flags.json).
Rollback: disabling feature flag removes enforcement immediately; audit enrichment is additive and does not require rollback.
